quests.title: Monkey Business on Kame Island
quests.summary: A tailed little boy from decades ago is wrecking Kame House. Roshi wants him calmed down before the moon rises.

brief.text: Ah, the new recruit! Good timing. A little boy with a monkey tail washed up this morning, and he's turned my house into kindling.
That's Goku. Well, an echo of Goku from when he was knee-high. He's glowing purple and yelling about being the strongest.
I'll come with you. Kid Goku nearly broke my nose the day we met, and back then he wasn't even trying.
And {name}, whatever you do, don't let him look at the moon. Trust an old man on this one.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Kame House at dusk. The beach is full of craters the size of bathtubs, and a pale moon is climbing over the sea.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Are you strong? You look strong! Grandpa's voice says I gotta beat everybody, so I'm gonna beat you!

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Grandpa's voice? Goku, your grandpa's been gone for years!

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Something is whispering to him. Let's shake it loose before that moon gets any higher.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Rock, scissors... nah. I'll just punch you!

win.speaker: narrator
win.text: The great ape topples into the surf and shrinks back into a soggy, sleepy boy.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Huh? Why's the beach all broken? ...Did I do that? Sorry, mister.

win.speaker: player2
win.text: He went ape the second the moon came out. Just like old times. I hate old times.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: There was a voice in the fog. It sounded like Grandpa, but meaner. It said my tail makes me special.

win.speaker: player
win.text: Fog over the ocean, using a dead man's voice. I'll keep an eye out.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Hehe! I win! Now you gotta give me your lunch!

after.text: Well done! Kame House is only mostly destroyed. That's better than average for a Goku visit.
That 'Grandpa voice' bothers me. Gohan was the gentlest man I ever trained. Someone is wearing his memory like a mask.

quests.title: The Gentlest Man I Ever Trained
quests.summary: Grandpa Gohan has walked out of the Other World with violet eyes. Roshi wants to know who showed him the way back.

brief.text: Fortuneteller Baba called. One of her fighters is missing from her palace: Gohan. My old student. Goku's grandfather.
He's been dead a long time, {name}. Dead men don't usually wander Mount Paozu looking for their grandson.
The Malice comes from Hell's machine. Maybe it's dragging the dead along with it.
Then bring him back gently. He taught that boy everything about kindness. Don't let anyone make him teach the opposite.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Mount Paozu. A halo flickers above an old man's head, half swallowed by violet smoke.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: You've come to take me back. I won't go. I was promised more years. The years with Goku I never got.

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Promised by who?

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: A kind voice, in a black mist. It said a man who loved so much deserved to keep living. Then why does it hurt?

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Forgive me, child. The Turtle School's Four Virtues... I can't remember a single one.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Ah... the fog is lifting. I can see the cottage. I can see where his crib used to be.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: That voice wasn't kind. It was hungry, and it was laughing the whole time it spoke.

win.speaker: player
win.text: Did it have a face?

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Small. Pointed ears. Old eyes in a young face. And it smelled of standing water, like a well nobody draws from.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Tell Roshi I'm sorry. And tell Goku... no. Don't tell him. Let him remember me smiling.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Stay down, child. I only want what that voice promised me.

after.text: Black mist and stagnant water... I've heard of something like that, long ago. Kami would know. He never liked talking about it.
Gohan's back at Baba's, safe. I told him you had a good heart. He said, 'Then you can't have been the one teaching them.' Rude!

quests.title: The Rice Cooker Problem
quests.summary: Demon King Piccolo has broken out of his old seal and taken the King's Castle. Time for the old master to go full power.

brief.text: Now that we know Garlic Jr. is behind all this, I have a confession. I'm something of an expert in seals. The Mafuba.
My master Mutaito died sealing Demon King Piccolo in a rice cooker. The Malice just cracked that cooker open like an egg.
So what's the plan?
The plan is that I take off my shirt. Don't make that face. This is serious martial arts.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: King's Castle. The throne room roof is gone, and something green is sitting on the throne.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: The old turtle. Mutaito's whelp. You look so frail. Did you come to apologize for the rice cooker?

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Hohoho. I came to put you back in it. Mind the shirt, {name}, it's vintage.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: This violet power answers to a little prince who thinks he owns me. I'll let him think so. Until I eat him.

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Garlic Jr. can't even keep his own monsters on a leash. Charming.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: This fog was the leash, wasn't it. And I let it bark for me. Unforgivable.

win.speaker: player2
win.text: Mutaito gave his life for one seal. I'm not about to waste it. Back in the jar with you, at least in spirit.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Laugh, turtle. Seals rot. The Dead Zone rotted, and that brat Garlic is the proof. Every prison opens eventually.

win.speaker: player2
win.text: Then we'll be waiting outside the door. That's what the Turtle School is for.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Pitiful. The turtle's shell cracks like any other.

after.text: Whew. My back. My knees. My everything. Still, I've got one more lesson in me, and you've earned all of them.
Come train at Kame House any time. Bring magazines. For the... morale of the student body.

quests.title: Homework Is Not Optional
quests.summary: Little Gohan has run into the woods glowing purple, and he still hasn't finished his math worksheet.

brief.text: You're the Patrol rookie? Good. My Gohan ran into the forest this morning and his eyes were PURPLE. And he left his math book on the table!
First that Piccolo kidnaps him, now some fog from Hell thinks it can raise my son? Not under my roof.
He might be young Gohan, from years ago. The Malice pulls echoes out of the past.
Then the past Gohan has homework too! Bring him home, {name}. Gently. Then tell him to sit at his desk.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Mount Paozu, by the river. A small boy sits on a rock, glowing violet and very, very angry.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: I'm not going back! Mom makes me study and Mr. Piccolo makes me run and nobody asks what I want!

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: That's a lot of anger for someone so small.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: The fog says I'm the strongest one in my family. It says I should make everyone stop bossing me around.

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Then let's see the strongest kid on Mount Paozu.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: I... I yelled at Mom. In my head I yelled such mean things.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: I'm sorry. I don't even hate studying. I just wish I could be a scholar AND protect everybody.

win.speaker: player
win.text: You can be both. Come on, your mom's waiting. With the math book.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Oh no. She's going to be so mad.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: See? I don't need anybody telling me what to do!

after.text: He's home, he's crying, and he's doing his fractions. Perfect. Thank you, {name}.
If you ever see purple fog near my house again, you come get me. I have a frying pan and I am not afraid to use it.

quests.title: Till Death Do Us Spar
quests.summary: Two young Gokus are brawling in the valley, and neither of them remembers Chichi. That will not stand.

brief.text: There are TWO Gokus in the valley. One looks like the day we married, one like when he came back from King Kai's. Both purple.
They're fighting each other! Laughing! And when I called to them, the younger one asked who I was.
He promised to marry me at the World Tournament. He doesn't get to forget that just because some fog told him to!
I'll remind them. With my fists, if that's all right.
That's how he learns best.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: A valley below Mount Paozu, at sunset. Two Gokus, years apart, trade blows and grin like madmen.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Hey, a new challenger! The fog says if I beat everyone, I never have to stop fighting. Sounds great!

intro.speaker: enemy2
intro.text: You look like you could last a while. Don't hold back, okay? I'm gonna use the Kaio-ken.

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Chichi says hello. And that you missed dinner. For a week.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Chichi...? That name feels warm. But the fog says warm things make you weak.

win.speaker: enemy2
win.text: Ow... that knocked the purple right out of my head. Huh. I'm starving.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Chichi! I promised her, at the tournament! I remember now. Aw jeez, she's gonna kill me.

win.speaker: player
win.text: Probably. But she'll feed you first.

win.speaker: enemy2
win.text: The fog kept saying fighting is all I am. That's not right. I fight so I can come home after.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: That was fun! Get up, let's go again! ...Hey, how come you're not getting up?

after.text: They ate eleven bowls each and fell asleep on the porch, snoring in harmony. Some things the Malice can't change.

quests.title: My Son Is Not a Weapon
quests.summary: Teen Gohan has gone Super Saiyan 2 and won't power down. Chichi blames the Cell Games, and maybe herself.

brief.text: I never wanted him to fight Cell. Nobody listened to me. Now there's a teenage Gohan out there, hair standing up, glowing purple.
They say he crushes anyone who comes near. That's not my boy. My boy cries when he steps on a beetle.
The Malice feeds on rage. He had a lot of it at the Cell Games.
Then you find the boy under all that anger and you bring him home. Promise me, {name}.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The Cell Games Arena, cracked and silent. A teenage boy stands at its center, lightning crawling over a gold-and-violet aura.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Another one who wants me to fight. Fine. I'm done holding back. Holding back got my dad killed.

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Your mom sent me. She's not asking you to fight.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Mom... She was right. She was always right. And I went anyway. So what does that make me?

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Don't answer. Just come at me. I want to feel how much stronger I've gotten.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: I can't stay angry. Every time I try, I see Mom's face.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: The fog said my power belongs to everyone who ever needed saving. That I'm a weapon, and a good weapon is never put away.

win.speaker: player
win.text: You're a person. People get to go home.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: ...Can you walk me back? I don't think I can fly straight right now.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Stay down. I don't want to hurt you more. I just... can't stop.

after.text: He apologized for the Cell Games. Years late, and from a boy who's already grown up somewhere else, but I'll take it. Thank you.

quests.title: The Frying Pan of Justice
quests.summary: Goku's Super Saiyan fury from Namek has crashed into Mount Paozu. Chichi grabs her old armor. You don't argue.

brief.text: I saw him from the window. Goku, the golden angry one from Namek. He looked at our house like it was Frieza.
I'm going with you. Don't argue. I won the Junior Division before you were a gleam in anyone's eye.
Chichi, he's a Super Saiyan.
And I'm his WIFE. One of those outranks the other, {name}, and it's not the hair.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Mount Paozu. The trees bend outward from a furious golden blaze streaked with violet.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Frieza... where are you hiding? I'll make you pay for Krillin. I'll make you ALL pay.

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Goku! You look at me! There is no Frieza here, there's laundry, and you are tracking mud through it!

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Get out of my way. Now I'm mad. Don't make me hurt you too.

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Hurt me? I'd like to see you try. {name}, take the left side. I'll take his ear.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Chi...chi? Ow. Was that a frying pan? Why is there a frying-pan shape in my head?

win.speaker: player2
win.text: Because I put it there! You scared me half to death, you big dummy!

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: I was back on Namek. Everybody was gone. The fog made it feel like it was still happening, forever.

win.speaker: player2
win.text: It's over. It's been over for years. Come home. Dinner's cold, and that's your fault too.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: I said get out of my way! I won't stop until Frieza's gone!

after.text: Now I'll teach you how to fight like a mother, {name}. It's not pretty and it doesn't let go.
Goku says I hit harder than Vegeta. I say that's because Vegeta never had to raise two Saiyans.

quests.title: Rematch With a Vegetable
quests.summary: Saibamen are sprouting all over the Wasteland. Yamcha has a score to settle, and would really like some backup.

brief.text: Hey, rookie! Got a minute? A bunch of Saibamen are popping out of the ground over by the canyon. Purple ones.
You probably don't know this, but a Saibaman once... look, it doesn't matter. It used a cheap trick. Self-destruct. Very rude.
Didn't it kill you?
Temporarily! I got better! Anyway, you go first and I'll be right behind you. Strategically behind you.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The Wasteland. Small green figures claw their way out of the soil, bulbous heads glowing violet.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Kkkee! Kkkehehehe!

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Yamcha, they're giggling at you.

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: ...He's hiding behind a rock back there. He says you're all cowards. Well. He mouthed it.

intro.speaker: enemy2
intro.text: Kkkkeeeee!

win.speaker: narrator
win.text: The last Saibaman wilts, and the violet glow drains out of it like water into sand.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Kke... kkee...

win.speaker: player
win.text: These aren't wild. Someone planted them in rows. Neat, straight rows.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Kkkehehehe! Kkkee!

after.text: Nice! I mean, I totally had that, but nice! ...Rows, though? Saibamen don't grow in rows. Somebody's farming them.

quests.title: The Saiyan Who Gardens
quests.summary: Yamcha tracked the Saibaman farm to its farmer: a big, bald, very Corrupted Saiyan who is proud of his crop.

brief.text: Found the farmer. Bald guy, mustache, about the size of a house. Watering Saibamen with a tiny can. Humming.
It's Nappa. The guy who... look, that's also a bad memory. A lot of my memories are bad, okay? It's the price of the front line.
You were on the front line?
I was on A line! Go get him. I'll guard the... parking. Of the... I'll be here.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: A field of turned soil in tidy rows. A huge Saiyan kneels between them with a tiny watering can.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Hey, careful! You're stepping on the sprouts. You know how hard it is to grow these on a dirtball planet?

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Why are you farming Saibamen?

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: The fog said an army's coming, and I get to be its general. Vegeta never let me be general.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Bah, enough chit-chat! Time to plow!

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Ugh. Lost to a nobody again. That's becoming a thing, isn't it.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: An army, the fog said. Everybody who ever got told no. Some little guy in the mist was making promises to every grunt in Hell.

win.speaker: player
win.text: A little guy?

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Never saw him. Heard him, though. Squeaky voice, big words, laughs like a kettle. Hey, can I keep the watering can?

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Hah! You'll make good fertilizer. Hey, that's actually a great idea.

after.text: An army of grunts from Hell. Okay. Okay, that's fine. I'm fine. Everything is fine.
Hey, {name}... ever feel like everyone's moving forward except you? No? Ha. Me neither. Forget I said it.

quests.title: The Wolf at Midnight
quests.summary: Yamcha wants to meet you in the Wasteland at midnight. Alone. He says he finally figured it all out.

brief.text: {name}. Come to the Wasteland tonight. Just you. Don't tell Krillin. Don't tell anybody.
I figured it out. Why I always lose. Why everyone leaves me behind. It's not me. It was never me.
Yamcha, there's something wrong with your eyes.
Ha! Ha ha. Wrong. Tonight. Alone.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The Wasteland at midnight. A lone figure sits on the rock where Yamcha the desert bandit used to wait for travelers.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: You came. Good. You're the only one who ever treats me like I matter, you know that?

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Yamcha, the fog is all over you.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: It found me after Nappa. It said: 'You were his first friend, and they left you in the dirt.' It was right.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Goku. Krillin. Tien. Even Chiaotzu! I'm done being the joke. Wolf Fang Fist, {name}. Let's see who gets left behind now.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Oh no. Oh no, no. What did I say? Tell me I didn't say all that out loud.

win.speaker: player
win.text: You said it. You also fought better than I've ever seen you fight.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: ...Yeah? Huh. That's the worst compliment I've ever gotten, and I'm keeping it.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: The voice knew my name. The desert, the bandit days, everything. Whoever's behind this has been reading all of us like books.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Who's in the dirt now? Huh? WHO?

after.text: So. Uh. Can we not put that one on Krillin's bounty board?
I'll teach you the Wolf Fang Fist. For real. A guy who's been knocked down this often learns a lot about getting back up.

quests.title: Contract on a Crane
quests.summary: Tao Pai Pai has accepted a contract on Tien's life. The client paid in coins nobody can identify.

brief.text: Tao Pai Pai is in the Rocky Area. The world's greatest assassin, and my old master's brother. He's here for me.
I'd face him alone, but he's glowing like the others. And I'm told the Patrol needs field experience.
Why does he want you dead?
He's an assassin. Someone paid. Find out who, {name}. I've made many enemies, but I'd like to know which one bought me.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The Rocky Area. A tall man in a pink robe stands atop a stone spire, braid swaying, utterly calm.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: A child. They send a child to stand between me and my fee. How insulting.

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Who hired you to kill Tien?

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Professionals do not name clients. But this one paid in advance, and the power came free with the contract.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Do not worry. I charge nothing extra for witnesses.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Impossible. Defeated twice in one lifetime. Or is it three? The violet haze makes it hard to count.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Fine. The client. Short. Cloaked. A voice like a spoiled prince. He paid in black metal coins that rusted away in sunlight.

win.speaker: player
win.text: Black metal?

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Stamped with a star I have never seen in any sky. I take contracts from anyone. I did not enjoy taking that one.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Hmph. Efficient. I will bill the client for your funeral as well.

after.text: A star nobody's seen and coins that rot in daylight. Not one of my old enemies, then. Something worse.
Thank you, {name}. Tien Shinhan doesn't forget a debt.

quests.title: The Silence of Chiaotzu
quests.summary: Chiaotzu's voice in Tien's head has gone quiet. Then Cyborg Tao came back, with Chiaotzu at his side.

brief.text: Chiaotzu and I talk without speaking. Always have. Three days ago, his voice in my head stopped.
Last night it came back. It wasn't him. It whispered in a language I don't know, like wind under a door.
Then Tao Pai Pai's other self showed up with him. The machine one. Revenge, he said. I want my friend back, {name}.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Rocky Area, night. A cyborg with a blade in his arm, and beside him a pale little figure with his eyes shut tight.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Tien sends a pet. Ah, well. I'll practice on the pet first. The new body must be tested.

intro.speaker: enemy2
intro.text: ...Tien? No. Not Tien. The voice says Tien always leaves me behind. Tien left me behind against Nappa.

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Chiaotzu, that voice is lying to you.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Of course it lies. It lies wonderfully. It promised me Tien's head and a body that never rusts.

win.speaker: enemy2
win.text: Tien? Tien! I can hear him again. He's yelling. He's crying, a little.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Bah. Steel and grudges. That's all it wanted from me. Something with no pride of its own feeds on mine.

win.speaker: enemy2
win.text: The whispers were in an old tongue. Kami-sama might know it. It sounded like a curse and a lullaby at once.

win.speaker: player
win.text: Do you remember a single word?

win.speaker: enemy2
win.text: Just one. Makyo. It said it over and over, like a name it was proud of.

lose.speaker: enemy2
lose.text: Go away! I'll make you stop moving! I'm good at that!

after.text: Makyo. I asked Roshi. He went very quiet and said some stars should stay dark.
Chiaotzu's sleeping. He keeps waking up to ask if I'm still there. I'll be there every time he asks.

quests.title: Third Eye, Open
quests.summary: Tambourine is hunting World Tournament fighters by name. Tien is next on the list, and he plans to be waiting.

brief.text: Tambourine. Demon King Piccolo's hound. He killed Krillin once, years ago, and now he's back with a list of names from the Tournament.
Mine is next. Then Chiaotzu's. I'm done hiding behind contracts and whispers. We fight him together, {name}.
You've been practicing something. I can see it in your stance.
The Neo Tri-Beam. If I fall, you finish it. If I win, you've seen it up close. That's a lesson either way.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The Rocky Area at noon. A winged demon crouches on a boulder, flipping through a crumpled tournament roster.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Tien Shinhan. Third eye, Crane School. The list says you're next. The list is never wrong.

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Your father's gone. Garlic Jr. is using you like a fork from a drawer. Walk away, Tambourine.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Garlic? That runt thinks he holds my leash. I hunt for my own clan. He only makes it taste better.

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Then you'll fall for your own clan. {name}, I'll open with the Tri-Beam. Don't let him get past us.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Bah... the fog's gone, and my appetite with it. How dull.

win.speaker: player2
win.text: Garlic Jr. hands out power like candy. Everyone who takes it ends up owing him.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: He doesn't own the rest of it, crane. The filth under Hell has a mind of its own now. It laughs when he isn't looking.

win.speaker: player2
win.text: ...Remember that, {name}. Then let's go have tea. My hands won't stop shaking.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Cross off another name. Who's next? Ah, yes. The little white one.

after.text: You've earned the Crane's lessons. Not the third eye. That doesn't come off.
I was an assassin once, {name}. The Malice keeps trying to remind me. Training you is how I answer it.

quests.title: Dam It, Pilaf!
quests.summary: The river below Namu's village has stopped flowing. Upstream, someone built a dam with Pilaf's face on it.

brief.text: Rookie of the Patrol. Forgive the intrusion. My village lives on the river that runs down this mountain. Yesterday it stopped.
I followed it upstream. There is a wall of steel across it. With a face on it. A small, blue, extremely smug face.
That sounds like Emperor Pilaf.
I know no emperors. I only know that children are drinking from puddles. Will you come?

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Mountain Road. A clanking robot stands atop a crude dam, waving a flag with Pilaf's face on it.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Behold! The Pilaf Reservoir! Every drop of water on this mountain now belongs to the future ruler of the world!

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: You're stealing a village's water.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Stealing? I'm INVESTING. Once they're thirsty enough they'll pay anything. Mai! Shu! Maximum smugness!

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Ahh! The controls! Shu, you pressed the shiny one again! I said never press the shiny one!

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Fine! Take your stupid water! It's gone all funny anyway. Black, like ink, and it whispers when you bottle it.

win.speaker: player
win.text: It whispers?

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Nice things! It says I'm a genius! Which I am! Ugh, forget it. Retreat! Strategic retreat!

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Hah! Bow before the Pilaf Reservoir! Admission is five thousand zeni a sip!

after.text: The river runs again. But you are right to frown. Near the dam the water had a dark sheen. Like oil, but cold.
I will watch it. My people have died of thirst before. They will not die of poison while I stand.

quests.title: The Black Water Elixir
quests.summary: Pilaf is selling bottled 'Evil Elixir' to anyone with zeni. The dark water is turning drinkers vicious.

brief.text: Travelers on the road have been fighting each other. Neighbors. Brothers. Each carried a little bottle of black water.
The label reads 'Pilaf's Evil Elixir: Be Your Worst Self Today!' I do not understand this marketing.
So he's bottling the river.
And something in it is bottling people. Find him. This time, break the machine. I do not ask you to be gentle.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Mountain Road at dusk. Crates of black bottles are stacked in a cave, humming faintly.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: You again! Doesn't matter! I've been drinking my own product and frankly I feel incredible!

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Pilaf, that water is the Malice.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: The water says it came from somewhere called the Dead Zone! It used to be a mist! Now it's a business! Mai, Shu, COMBINE!

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: My elixir empire... crumbled like a cheap cookie.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: That water seeped out of a little crack in the rock. It smelled like an old well. The voice in it never gave a name.

win.speaker: player
win.text: Did it want something?

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: It wanted the whole world to drink. Even I thought that was a bit much, and I'm extremely evil!

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Hahaha! Have a free sample! Customer satisfaction guaranteed!

after.text: The Dead Zone. The old monks of the north speak of it. A prison with no outside. Something has leaked out of it.
I sealed the crack with stones from the temple. It will not hold forever. Nothing holds forever.

quests.title: The Devil Reads Hearts
quests.summary: Namu seeks Baba's demon fighter Akuman, whose beam strikes only evil hearts. The demon has become what he hunts.

brief.text: There is a fighter at Fortuneteller Baba's palace. A devil whose beam harms only the wicked. I wished to borrow his gift.
With it, we could test the water and the travelers, and know who carries the Malice. But Akuman has become what he hunts.
Then we beat him first and ask nicely after.
I would have said it with more ceremony. But yes. I will fight beside you.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The Desert under the stars. A grinning devil with a pitchfork floats above the sand, his skin flickering violet.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Ohoho! Visitors! Let me read your hearts. The Devilmite Beam never misses a wicked one.

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Akuman. We came to ask for your help.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Help? I judged the wicked for centuries. Now the fog says everyone is wicked. Everyone! It's so liberating!

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Then judge me first. I have carried water up this mountain since I was a boy. Find the evil in that.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Ow. Ow. Being on the receiving end of righteousness is the worst.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Fine, fine, I'll test your water. But listen. That Malice isn't only Hell's sludge. It has a second taste. Older.

win.speaker: player2
win.text: Older how?

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Like a mist sealed away for ages until it went sour. Someone stirred his own poison into Hell's. A true artist. I'm almost jealous.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Wicked, wicked, all of you wicked! Devilmite Beam!

after.text: Akuman will judge the river at each new moon. A strange alliance. My village has had stranger guests.
You have fought for my people three times, {name}. Let me teach you to fight for yours. We begin with the Cross Arm Dive.

quests.title: Senzu Larceny
quests.summary: A bag of senzu beans went missing from Korin's Tower, and Yajirobe swears he didn't eat them. This time.

brief.text: Oi! Patrol kid. Somebody swiped a whole bag of senzu off Korin's Tower, and the old cat thinks it was me.
Which is insulting! I only ate, like, four. The rest got nabbed by two weirdos in shoulder pads. Purple ones, with scouters.
Frieza's soldiers, on Earth?
Dunno, don't care. Get the beans back and we split 'em. Fifty-fifty. Sixty-forty. You get one.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The Desert. Two soldiers in Frieza Force armor are arguing over a little cloth bag.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: My scouter reads these beans at a power level of zero, yet they heal anything. Lord Frieza will promote us for this!

intro.speaker: enemy2
intro.text: The fog said we'd be officers. Officers! No more scrubbing the pods!

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Those beans belong to Korin. And a little bit to Yajirobe's stomach.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: A witness! Eliminate it!

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Promotion... cancelled...

win.speaker: enemy2
win.text: We just wanted to stop being nobodies. A voice in the mist promised a new empire. Bigger than Frieza's.

win.speaker: player
win.text: Bigger than Frieza's? Whose?

win.speaker: enemy2
win.text: It didn't say. Only that every soldier who ever died for Frieza would get to serve someone better. We'd have believed anything.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Ha! Your power level was barely worth recording!

after.text: You got 'em back? Great. Count's a little low. Don't look at me. Okay, look at me, but don't judge.
A new empire, huh? Every few years somebody wants one. Never anybody who shares their lunch.

quests.title: The Tail That Got Away
quests.summary: Young Vegeta remembers exactly who cut off his tail. So does the Malice. Yajirobe is hiding in a barrel.

brief.text: Hide me. HIDE ME. Vegeta's back. The old one, with the armor and the scouter. Yelling my name across the whole desert.
Years ago I sliced his tail off with my sword. Saved everyone's lives! He never even sent a thank-you card.
You want me to fight Vegeta so you don't have to.
Now you're thinking like a samurai! Also, if it gets dark, don't look at the moon. And don't let HIM look at it either.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The Desert under a fat, round moon. A Saiyan prince stands on a dune, his scouter flashing.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Where is he? The fat one with the sword. The fog says he's here. I'll take his head and my tail back with it.

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: That's not how tails work.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Silence, insect! You're beneath me, and so is he.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: No... look up. A full moon. Perfect. Now you'll understand what a Saiyan truly is.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Agh... curse it. Beaten by a nobody with the moon in the sky. This never happened.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Something used me. Me! The prince of all Saiyans, a puppet for a voice that giggled. I'll find it and tear it apart.

win.speaker: player
win.text: Get in line.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: I AM the line. And tell that coward with the sword this isn't over.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Pathetic. Now bring me the fat one, and maybe I'll let you crawl away.

after.text: Is he gone? He's gone. I knew you could do it. I was supervising the whole time. From the barrel.

quests.title: Every Vegeta Wants My Head
quests.summary: Three Vegetas from three different years heard Yajirobe bragging. Yajirobe has decided to fight. Mostly.

brief.text: So I MAY have been at a noodle stand telling the tail story. Loudly. And the Malice MAY have been listening. Now there's three of him.
Regular Vegeta. Golden Vegeta. Extra-spiky golden Vegeta. All saying my name like it's a swear word.
Then come with me this time.
...Fine. FINE. But only because Korin says if I don't, he's cutting off my senzu forever. I'm doing this for the beans.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The Desert at noon. Three Vegetas stand in a row, each scowling in a different shade of gold and violet.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: So the tail thief finally crawls out of his hole. With a bodyguard. How fitting.

intro.speaker: enemy2
intro.text: I'll take the bodyguard. The fat one has been bragging about me for years. He's mine.

intro.speaker: enemy3
intro.text: Enough talk. You're both trash, and I've waited long enough to take out the trash.

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Okay, okay, I'm scared, but I got a sword and a belly full of courage. Mostly rice. Let's go!

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Tch. Beaten by a rookie and a glutton. If Kakarot hears of this, I'll destroy the planet.

win.speaker: player2
win.text: I won't tell him nothin'! Unless he pays. Senzu accepted.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Garlic Jr. Of all the insects in the universe, a dwarf from a sealed box made me his weapon. Three times over.

win.speaker: player
win.text: Well, he's not getting a fourth.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Hmph. And you, samurai. ...It was a clean cut. I'll admit that much. Tell anyone and you die.

lose.speaker: enemy3
lose.text: That's it? That's the sword that humiliated a prince? Pathetic.

after.text: Did you hear that? 'A clean cut.' Vegeta complimented me. I'm getting that sentence framed.
Fine, I'll teach you. Lesson one: eat first. Lesson two: hit 'em while they're talking. That's the whole school, really.

quests.title: Ncha! The General Hates Tag
quests.summary: A grumpy man in a Red Ribbon uniform is floating houses around Penguin Village. Arale wants to play with him.

brief.text: Ncha! Hiya! Are you the new Patrol person? Your outfit is so cool! Wanna see me crack the planet? Kidding! Mostly!
There's a grumpy blond man in town floating houses with his brain! He's all purple and sparkly. I asked to play tag and he yelled.
That's General Blue of the Red Ribbon Army. He's dangerous.
Ooh, dangerous tag is the best kind! You go first! I'll be It! Ncha!

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Penguin Village. Houses drift gently above the road, and a man in a blue uniform scowls at a penguin in a hat.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: This village is an insult to discipline. Everything here talks. The penguins talk!

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: General Blue, the Malice has you. Stand down.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: The Red Ribbon Army is finished, but the voice in the mist says I can lead a new army. One that never retreats.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: And it begins by flattening this ridiculous town. Prepare yourself!

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Unbelievable. Defeated in this town. Again. Is it the air? It's the air, isn't it.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: That little girl. Glasses. Where is she? If she comes near me, I'm leaving the planet.

win.speaker: player
win.text: She wants to play tag.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: ...I would sooner face Commander Red's firing squad, thank you.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Hmph. Discipline wins. Now, where is that dreadful child?

after.text: Aww, he flew away screaming! Did I win tag? I think I won tag! Ncha!
Come back soon! Gatchan and I are making a new friend who's really, REALLY big! Kidding! Or not!

quests.title: A Big Friend for Arale
quests.summary: Arale heard a robot giant lives in Muscle Tower. She's sure they'll be best friends. He's sure he has to fight you.

brief.text: Guess what! A big robot lives in a tower in the snow! A ROBOT, like me! We're gonna be best friends, I just know it!
But people say he's angry and purple now. Maybe he's lonely! I get lonely when Senbei works all night.
That's Android 8. Hatchan. He's actually very gentle.
Then let's go hug him! You do the fighting part. I'm bad at stopping.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Muscle Tower, half buried in snow. A huge, kind-faced android stands on the top floor, fists trembling.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Go away. Hatchan hurt people before. Doctor made Hatchan. Doctor said fight. Now voice says fight. Always fight.

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: You don't have to listen to any voice but yours.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Hatchan's voice... small. Other voice... big. It says Goku forgot Hatchan. It says nobody comes back for Hatchan.

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: A girl came all the way from Penguin Village to be your friend. That's somebody coming back.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Hatchan... sorry. Hatchan not want to hurt. Hatchan just very, very cold.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Friend girl came? For Hatchan? Hatchan never had robot friend.

win.speaker: player
win.text: She's outside building a snowman taller than the tower. You'll like her.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Voice in mist laughed when Hatchan cried. Hatchan does not like that voice. Hatchan will remember it.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Hatchan... sorry. Please stay down. Please.

after.text: Hatchan's my best friend now! He let me ride on his shoulders! He's coming to Penguin Village for the wrestling tournament!
Wrestling tournament? Oh yeah! I didn't tell you! I'm throwing one! Ncha!

quests.title: Penguin Village Pro-Wrestling Grand Prix
quests.summary: Arale's wrestling tournament has drawn real challengers: three members of the Ginyu Force, who think it's an invasion.

brief.text: The tournament is ON! We've got a ring and snacks and a judge who's a talking sun! And three funny guys in matching outfits signed up!
They keep striking poses and yelling their names! They say they're here to conquer the planet! What a cool entrance!
Arale, that's the Ginyu Force. And they're Corrupted.
So they're the bad guys! Every tournament needs bad guys! Get in the ring, {name}! I'll do the commentary!

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Penguin Village, a wrestling ring strung with candy-colored ropes. Three Ginyu Force members strike a pose so hard the ground cracks.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Guldo!

intro.speaker: enemy2
intro.text: Burter!

intro.speaker: enemy3
intro.text: Jeice! Together we are the... hang on. We're two short. The pose doesn't work with three. Recoome and the Captain are late!

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Do you want to wait for them, or...

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Never! A Ginyu Force member never waits! Even if the pose is incomplete! ...It's very incomplete.

win.speaker: enemy3
win.text: Blimey. The violet stuff made our poses really crisp, I'll give it that. Shame about the losing.

win.speaker: enemy2
win.text: Nobody's ever been faster than me. The voice promised we'd be the elite of a new empire. Under a new star.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: The Captain got the same offer. He said yes before he heard the pay. That's the Captain for you.

win.speaker: player
win.text: Where is he now?

win.speaker: enemy3
win.text: Rehearsing a new pose. Says it's for the final. Bring a camera, mate. And bandages.

lose.speaker: enemy2
lose.text: Too slow! Nobody's faster than the great Burter!

after.text: That was the BEST match! And the judge gave you ten points for style! The sun is a really tough judge!
The Captain's coming! I'm so excited I could crack the planet in half! Kidding! ...Hold my glasses.

quests.title: Pose-Off for the Universal Belt
quests.summary: Captain Ginyu and Recoome arrive for the final with a new pose and a body-swap plan. Arale is tagging in.

brief.text: It's the final! Captain Ginyu and the big orange one, Recoome! And I'm your tag partner! We need a team pose! Ncha!
Okay, I made one up. I point at the sky, you point at me, and we both yell 'Ncha!' It's perfect.
Ginyu can swap bodies with people. Be careful.
Ooh, swapping! Like trading lunches! I'll trade my lunch, but not my glasses. I can't see a thing without my glasses.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Penguin Village, the grand final. The crowd is three penguins, a policeman and a talking sun. It is loud anyway.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Captain Ginyu! Leader of the Ginyu Force! And I have choreographed a new pose for the empire to come!

intro.speaker: enemy2
intro.text: Recoooome! Recoome loves wrestling! Recoome will hug you until you pop!

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Ncha! Arale! The strongest girl in Penguin Village! And this is {name}! The coolest!

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Enough! Your body will make a fine vessel, robot girl. Body... CHANGE!

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Huh? That tickled. Did something happen? Your face looks really surprised.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: My Body Change bounced off a machine. My new pose was flawless and still I lost. Worst day of my career.

win.speaker: enemy2
win.text: Recoome... sleepy. Recoome had fun, though. Little girl hits harder than Vegeta.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Listen, you. The voice that recruited us has a star. A red star, swinging toward this planet. When it arrives, nobody will be posing.

win.speaker: player2
win.text: A star coming here? Ooh, I could catch it! Kidding! Unless?

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Behold the beauty of victory! Pose, Recoome! The SPECIAL pose!

after.text: We won the belt! It's made of candy! I already ate half! You can have the half with the bite marks!
Now I'll teach you pro-wrestling! Lesson one is be super strong. Lesson two is also be super strong. Ncha!

quests.title: Ashes of Guru's Children
quests.summary: Zarbon and Dodoria are burning Namekian villages again, as if Frieza's invasion never ended.

brief.text: Patroller. I am Nail, guardian of Elder Guru. I will be brief: Frieza's lieutenants are on Namek, and they are burning villages.
Zarbon the vain and Dodoria the butcher. The same two who came before. My people are dying a second time.
And you have to stay by Guru's side?
The first time, I did. It was my duty. It was also my shame. Not again. Go ahead of me; I will guard the survivors.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Planet Namek. Smoke rises from a village of white domes. Two of Frieza's men stand among the ruins.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Oh, a visitor. Dodoria, do try not to splash anything on my cape this time.

intro.speaker: enemy2
intro.text: Hah! Look at it, all brave! I'll squash it like those Namekian brats. Same as last time!

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: There won't be a last time. There's only this time.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: How tiresome. I shall be beautiful about this, and then I shall be ugly. You won't enjoy either.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: My face... the fog made me so lovely. Without it I feel almost... small.

win.speaker: enemy2
win.text: Ugh. We came back on orders. Not Frieza's. Some new boss whose voice crawls out of the mist.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: He promised us every world Frieza ever burned. He seemed to think we'd find that tempting.

win.speaker: player
win.text: Did you?

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Of course. That's why he chose us. He chooses people who've already done it once.

lose.speaker: enemy2
lose.text: Hahaha! Just like the Namekians! Pop, pop, pop!

after.text: The villagers are safe. I carried the last child out myself. I needed that more than I can say.
Frieza's men, serving a new master. Elder Guru is troubled. He dreams of a red star he cannot name.

quests.title: A Coward's Bargain
quests.summary: Frieza's soldier Cui offers to sell what he knows about the Malice in exchange for safe passage. What could go wrong?

brief.text: A soldier named Cui has come to the village under a white flag. He says he knows who is behind the Malice.
He will speak only to the Patrol. He wants a pardon, a ship and, in his words, 'a little respect for once.'
Do you trust him?
I trust that he is afraid. A frightened man tells you the truth or betrays you, depending on the hour. Keep your guard up.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: A ridge on Namek. A purple soldier waits beside a white flag, tapping his scouter nervously.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Ah, the Patrol. I'll talk. Everything I know. The one behind it has eyes everywhere, and his star is... wait, is that a camera?

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: There's no camera. Talk.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Hahaha! Of course there isn't. Because there's no deal! He promised me more than a pardon! He promised me VEGETA!

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Revenge on the prince who blew me apart! All I had to do was lure you somewhere quiet. Sorry, rookie!

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Ugh. Fine. FINE. Betraying people is much harder than Lord Frieza made it look.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Here's the real truth. He's been buying star charts from Frieza's old archive. Hunting a wandering star. The Makyo Star.

win.speaker: player
win.text: What happens when it gets here?

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: He gets stronger. Whoever he is. I never saw him. Just a small shadow, and black water pooling where he stood.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Ha! Got you! Wait, do I still get paid if I only did this part? Hello? Voice?

after.text: So Cui told the truth in the end. Fear always chooses eventually.
The Makyo Star. Elder Guru spoke the name once, waking from a fever. Then he made me promise to forget it. I could not.

quests.title: The Fight Nail Never Finished
quests.summary: Frieza, in three forms, has come back to Namek. Nail fought him once and lost. This time he means to win.

brief.text: Frieza is here. Three of him. The form that broke my arm, and the forms that came after, when he grew bored.
When I fought him, I was only stalling, buying time for Gohan and Krillin. I never fought to win. I want to know how that feels.
Then we fight to win. Together.
Together. Guru would like that. He always said I fought too much alone.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Namek, under a bruise-colored sky. Frieza floats above a field of broken pillars, smiling.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Oh my. The Namekian who wasted my afternoon. Have you come to stall again? I do so love a performance.

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Not this time. This time I fight to finish you.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Finish me? Something in this marvelous fog has the nerve to whisper orders to me. To ME. When I'm done here, I'll find it.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: But first, a lesson in manners. I'll be gentle. For a moment.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: This is intolerable. Beaten AND puppeted. Which offends me more? I truly cannot decide.

win.speaker: player2
win.text: It is done. I stood my ground, and I won. Guru... did you see?

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Enjoy it, slug. That little toad with the star thinks he can command an emperor. When I find him, I won't be using words.

win.speaker: player
win.text: Get in line, Frieza.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Oh, did you fall down? How charming. Do get up. I'd hate for this to end so quickly.

after.text: I have fought Frieza and won. I do not feel proud. I feel finished, as if a long debt has been paid.
Train with me, {name}. I will teach you what I learned stalling a tyrant: how to stand when standing is all you have.

quests.title: Celipa's Last Order
quests.summary: Bardock's old crew died on Planet Meat. Now Celipa is back from Hell, Corrupted, and she blames him.

brief.text: Patrol, huh? I don't need a babysitter. But there's a woman out past the asteroid belt in my old crew's armor. Celipa.
She died on Planet Meat with the others. Dodoria's men butchered them while I was out cold. I found them in the mud.
Now she's alive and purple and screaming my name on every channel. Go see. I'll be close.
You won't come?
I can't look at her. Not yet. Go.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Outer Space, near a dead moon. A Saiyan woman in battered armor hovers among the wreckage of an attack pod.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Bardock sent a kid? Figures. He sent us to Planet Meat, too. Said it'd be easy. Said he'd catch up.

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: He found you. Afterward. He's never forgotten.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: He wasn't THERE! Tora, Borgos, Shugesh, me. We died calling his name. The fog brought back every second of it.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: So I'll start with you. Then I'll show him what it feels like to wait for someone who never comes.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Damn. Rookie hits like a Saiyan. Or like a Saiyan wishes they did.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Tell him... tell him we know he tried. I knew it then. The fog chewed it up and spat it back out as hate.

win.speaker: player
win.text: You could tell him yourself.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: No. Not like this. And tell him something else. In Hell, the old Saiyans whisper about a voice promising a new Planet Vegeta.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Stay down. Bardock always said that's what weak soldiers do best.

after.text: She said that? That we tried? ...Huh. Give me a minute.
I still see things, you know. Ever since that Kanassan hit me. Lately it's a red star no one's charted, and something small laughing under it.

quests.title: Disappointment of the House
quests.summary: Bardock's eldest son Raditz is rampaging through the shipping lanes. Bardock decides it's time for family business.

brief.text: Raditz. My eldest. He's out there knocking freighters around, glowing like the rest. Of course he is.
Kid always wanted to be top-class. Never was. Neither was I, but I didn't whine about it.
You want me to fight your son?
I want you to knock some sense into my son. Then I'll have a word with him. It's been a few decades.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Outer Space. A long-haired Saiyan crushes a freighter's hull in one hand, laughing at the alarms.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Ha! The fog was right. I AM top-class! Kakarot, Vegeta, Nappa, none of them can look down on me now!

intro.speaker: player
intro.text: Your father's watching.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Father? Bardock? ...Where? No. No, let him watch. Let him finally see what I am.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Here's a present for you, rookie! And if that's not enough, there's a moon over there with my name on it!

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: I lost? Again? With all that power? Then what was the point of any of it.

win.speaker: narrator
win.text: A scarred Saiyan in green armor drifts down beside his fallen son. For a long moment, neither speaks.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: ...He said 'idiot' and put his hand on my head. Like when I was small. I hate him. I really don't.

win.speaker: player
win.text: The voice that gave you this power. What did it ask for?

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Nothing yet. That's what scared me. It said it would collect when its star rose.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Begone! Ha! See that, father? Did you SEE that?!

after.text: Raditz is a lousy fighter and a worse son. He's also mine. Thanks for not killing him.
His star. My star. Celipa's voice. It's the same thing, Patrol. Somebody's building a Saiyan army out of our worst days.

quests.title: The King Who Knelt
quests.summary: King Vegeta has risen from Hell to crown himself again. Bardock has opinions about the king who sold his people to Frieza.

brief.text: King Vegeta. Last king of the Saiyans. He knelt to Frieza, handed over his own son as a hostage, and called it strategy.
Now he's back, purple-eyed, gathering Saiyan ghosts in a crater on dead Earth, calling it the new Planet Vegeta.
You don't like him.
I don't need to like him. I need him to stop recruiting my dead friends. Let's go pay our respects to His Majesty.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: A ruined Earth. In a crater shaped like a throne room, a bearded Saiyan king sits on a heap of broken armor.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Bardock. The low-class soldier who flew at Frieza alone. I remember you. You embarrassed me.

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: And you knelt. Right before he blew us all up, you knelt. I remember that too.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: I knelt to save my people! I failed. Now a voice in the mist offers a planet that can never be destroyed. Kneel, and I forgive you.

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: I've never knelt once in my life. Not starting for a dead king. {name}, let's take his crown.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Enough. The fog is gone, and the shame is still here. It was always going to be here.

win.speaker: player2
win.text: Frieza fooled you. He fooled all of us. Some of us just didn't kneel while it happened.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: My son. I gave him to Frieza as a child. The fog showed me what became of him. A wizard's mark on his brow. A demon's light in his eyes.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Bardock... find him. Free him. I have no right to ask it. I am asking.

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: Kneel, low-class. Every Saiyan kneels to his king in the end.

after.text: Never thought I'd take an order from that man. Never thought he'd say 'asking.'

quests.title: A Prince's Mark
quests.summary: King Vegeta's son wears Babidi's mark, and a future version of him burns with crimson fur. The father wants this fight.

brief.text: Found the prince. Two of him. One with Babidi's M on his forehead, one from some far future with red fur and eyes like a wolf.
King Vegeta's going in with you. Yeah, I said it. The old man walked out of Hell on his own to do this. Respect that.
And you?
I'm watching the perimeter. Something's been circling this fight. Big. Hungry. Not Garlic Jr. Something even he never controlled.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The World Tournament Stage at sunset. A prince with an M on his brow stands where he once betrayed everyone he loved.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: Father. Of all the ghosts. You sold me to Frieza, and now you've come to lecture me about my choices?

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: I've come to fight you. It is the only language our family ever spoke well.

intro.speaker: enemy2
intro.text: Hmph. Ancient history. I'm the strongest Vegeta who ever lived. Neither of you even registers.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: The fog says I can finally be as cruel as I truly am. No more pretending. No more family. Only pride.

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Then let me show you what pride is worth. Patroller, stay at my side. I will not fail a son twice.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: ...Father. You fought for me. You never did that. Not once.

win.speaker: player2
win.text: I was a fool and a coward. I knelt. You never have. Be better than me, boy. You already are.

win.speaker: enemy2
win.text: Tch. Sentimental garbage. ...The Malice has slipped Garlic's leash entirely, by the way. Something underneath bit through. I felt it.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: Kakarot hears none of this. Understood?

lose.speaker: enemy
lose.text: You see, father? This is what you made. Be proud.

after.text: Watched from the ridge. The king put his hand on the prince's head, and the prince let him. Strangest thing I ever saw, and I've seen the future.
One more thing to settle, Patrol. Mine. When you're ready.

quests.title: Final Revenge
quests.summary: Mecha Frieza and King Cold have crawled out of the Malice's last tide. Bardock has waited a lifetime for this fight.

brief.text: Frieza's metal shell and his father, King Cold. The two who decided the Saiyans weren't worth keeping. They're out there.
I flew at Frieza once with nothing but rage. Didn't scratch him. Watched my planet burn in the light of my own last blast.
This time I've got a partner. Don't make me regret saying that.
For Celipa. For Tora. For Planet Vegeta.
...Yeah. For them. Let's go.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Outer Space. A great horned king and his half-machine son wait on the drifting wreck of Frieza's flagship.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: A Saiyan. Look, Frieza, a Saiyan. I thought we'd gotten rid of those.

intro.speaker: enemy2
intro.text: Father, that's Bardock. The monkey who tried to stop me with a little ball of light. I never forgot his face.

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Good. Then you'll recognize it when it's the last thing you see.

intro.speaker: enemy
intro.text: The Malice gave us bodies again, little monkey. It gave us everything. Except a reason to fear you.

intro.speaker: player2
intro.text: Here's your reason. This one's for all of us, Frieza!

win.speaker: enemy2
win.text: Again... a Saiyan... again. This galaxy is infested.

win.speaker: enemy
win.text: No one rules the overflow now. It just uses whatever monster is nearest. How humiliating to be the nearest.

win.speaker: player2
win.text: Ha. Hahaha. Celipa, you see that? Tora? Got 'em. Finally got 'em.

win.speaker: player
win.text: Bardock, are you crying?

win.speaker: player2
win.text: Space dust. Shut up, Patrol. ...Thanks.

lose.speaker: enemy2
lose.text: Just like Planet Vegeta. Just like your little world. Pop.

after.text: My visions stopped. First time in years. No red star, no laughing, no burning planets. Just quiet.
I'll teach you, {name}. Low-class style. You don't win because you were born strong. You win because you refuse to stop.

0.greet: Hey! Wanna learn the Kaio-ken? King Kai taught me. It hurts a lot at first. Then it hurts a lot more, but you're way faster!
0.done: That's all I've got! Man, you're tough. Let's spar again tomorrow, okay? And the day after!

1.greet: I trained at a hundred times gravity on the way to Namek. We'll start lighter. Like, fifty.
1.done: You got it! And when you need a Spirit Bomb, just ask everybody for a little energy. They always help.

2.greet: I don't like this form much. It came from being angry. If you learn it, learn to stay in control. That's the hard part.
2.done: You stayed calm the whole time. Better than I did on Namek. I'm proud of you.

11.greet: Grandpa taught me to bow before a fight! So bow! Okay, now I hit you!
11.done: Wow, you learned all my moves! Wanna go fishing? I'm hungry. Are you hungry? I'm hungry.

12.greet: GRRRAAAHH! (The giant ape pounds the earth, then waits. It seems to want you to roar back.)
12.done: (The great ape thumps its chest once, softly, and curls up to sleep under the moon. Lessons over.)

13.greet: Mr. Piccolo left me alone in the wilderness for six months. I'll teach you what I learned! Mostly how not to get eaten.
13.done: You did great! Um, please don't tell my mom I taught you the Masenko. She thinks I only teach math.

14.greet: Dad and I trained in the Time Chamber for a year. He says I'm stronger than him. I'm still not sure I believe it.
14.done: That's everything. Just... promise me you'll only fight when you really have to.

15.greet: We stayed Super Saiyan all day, every day, until it felt like breathing. That's the trick: make power ordinary.
15.done: You can hold it without straining now. Dad would say you're ready for anything.

16.greet: This power came from losing control. I want you to learn it without that. It's harder, but it's the right way.
16.done: You never once let the anger take over. I wish I'd managed that against Cell.

24.greet: Stand. Again. Again. A Namekian warrior is measured not by how hard he strikes, but by how long he remains standing.
24.done: You are not Namekian, but you fight like one who protects. Elder Guru would bless you if he could see this.

25.greet: Me? A master? Wow. Okay. Rule one: Solar Flare first, questions later. Rule two: always duck. Seriously. Always.
25.done: You learned the Destructo Disc! Just watch where you throw it. I've nearly lost a few toes.

26.greet: The Wolf Fang Fist is all rhythm. Hah! Hah! Hah! Fight like a wolf: fast, low, and never in a straight line.
26.done: You're a natural! Okay, maybe better than me. Don't tell anyone. Especially Krillin.

27.greet: The Crane School taught me to kill. Roshi taught me why not to. I'll teach you both halves, and you'll choose.
27.done: The Neo Tri-Beam costs everything you have. Use it only for someone worth that price.

28.greet: I can't punch very hard. So I make people stop moving instead! Telekinesis takes focus. And snacks.
28.done: You did it! Tien says you're a good student. He never says that about anybody. Except me.

29.greet: You want the prince of all Saiyans to train you? Fine. Keep up or be left behind, insect. I won't slow down.
29.done: Hmph. You're no longer completely worthless. Don't let it go to your head.

30.greet: Under the moon, a Saiyan becomes what he truly is. Try not to be crushed while you learn what that means.
30.done: Enough. You survived my true form. Few can say that, and most of them aren't alive to say it.

34.greet: I don't train students. I train rivals. If you aren't trying to surpass me, get off my battlefield.
34.done: Tch. You've learned it all. Now train until you can beat me, then come back so I can beat you.

35.greet: A Super Saiyan's power means nothing without precision. Every blast, every step. Again. Wrong. Again.
35.done: Perfect form. ...Don't make me repeat that. I said it once.

36.greet: Kakarot thinks power is fun. It isn't. It's a debt you pay every day in sweat. Start paying.
36.done: You've paid. You've earned every technique I have. Now stop staring at me.

37.greet: I let a wizard into my head so I could fight Kakarot as my old self. Learn what I learned: pride is a blade with no handle.
37.done: You've seen the worst of me and trained anyway. Final Explosion is the last lesson. Pray you never need it.

38.greet: This form took a machine, a tail and Bulma's genius. You only have to survive me. That's harder.
38.done: Final Shine Attack. Remember that feeling. It's what being a prince is supposed to feel like.

60.greet: Training? Ugh. Fine. But we eat first, and you're buying. Samurai rule number one: never fight hungry.
60.done: That's everything I know. Took you five lessons. Took me five meals. Same thing, really.

66.greet: The Turtle School way: work hard, study well, eat and rest plenty, and enjoy life. Especially the enjoying part. Hohoho!
66.done: You've mastered the original Kamehameha. Took me fifty years to invent that. Show some respect. And some magazines.

67.greet: When the shirt comes off, it's serious. Don't laugh. I can blow up the moon. I HAVE blown up the moon.
67.done: That's the MAX POWER Kamehameha. Now help me get my shirt back on. Something in my shoulder went pop.

68.greet: Gentleness is a technique too. A strong man who cannot be kind has only learned half the art. Shall we begin?
68.done: You fight with an open heart. Goku did too, even as a baby. Thank you for letting an old ghost teach again.

69.greet: I fought at the Tournament for water. I will teach you to fight for something larger than yourself. Begin by kneeling.
69.done: The Cross Arm Dive is yours. Carry it to whoever is thirsty, whatever it is they thirst for.

70.greet: Hatchan strong. Hatchan careful, too. Hatchan teach you both. Careful first.
70.done: You learned everything! Hatchan happy! Goku would be happy too. Hatchan will tell him.

71.greet: I am the king of all Saiyans. Dead, disgraced, but king. You will address me as such while I teach you.
71.done: You fight like a Saiyan noble. Few deserve that praise. Fewer still have heard it from me.

72.greet: The royal ape is no beast. It is a king who no longer has to pretend to be civilized. Watch closely.
72.done: Enough. You have learned what it means to fight with the moon at your back.

73.greet: Low-class style: no fancy stances, no secret scrolls. You hit, you get hit, you get up. Ready?
73.done: That's all of it. Now go change somebody's future. I couldn't change mine. Maybe you'll do better.

74.greet: A Great Ape is a weapon. Most Saiyans let it do their thinking. I'll teach you to stay awake inside it.
74.done: You kept your head the whole time. Celipa never managed that. Neither did I, most nights.

75.greet: Bardock's crew fought dirty and fought together. You get to learn one of those. Pick fast.
75.done: Not bad, kid. If you'd been on Planet Meat, maybe we'd have come home. Probably not. But maybe.

76.greet: Great Ape dance class. Step on the enemy, not on me. Simple.
76.done: You'd have made a fine Saiyan. Loud, stubborn, always hungry. Tora would've liked you.

77.greet: I am a top-class warrior! ...Fine, not top-class. But I can still teach you more than Kakarot ever could.
77.done: You've mastered my techniques. Don't tell my father. He'll say I finally did something right and I'll never hear the end of it.

78.greet: Every Saiyan can transform. Not every Saiyan can aim. Let's fix the second part.
78.done: Good. Now you know the moon's secret. Guard it. Earthlings keep blowing theirs up.

79.greet: Kkkee! Kkkehehe! (The Saibaman points at your chest, then at itself, then mimes a very large explosion.)
79.done: Kkkeee... (It offers you a seed. You decide not to plant it.)

80.greet: Training? Ha! Okay, rule one: the big guy wins. Rule two: if the big guy loses, hit harder.
80.done: Hey, you got all of it! Vegeta never said I'd make a good teacher. Guess he was wrong. Don't tell him I said that.

81.greet: Great Ape's easy. You get big. You smash. I don't get why everybody makes it complicated.
81.done: Smashed everything! Perfect student. Wanna go throw some mountains?

82.greet: Grace first, then force. An ugly victory is still a defeat, darling. Shoulders back.
82.done: Elegant. Truly. You may tell others I trained you. Do mention the hair.

83.greet: This form is hideous and I despise it. It is also very, very strong. Learn it, and never let me see you enjoy it.
83.done: Yes, yes, you're a monster now too. Go away before I need a mirror.

84.greet: Hah! You wanna learn from me? Then you'd better like pain. I like it fine, as long as it's yours.
84.done: Ugh, you learned it all. Fine. Get lost before I get hungry.

85.greet: Yes, yes, I'm a coward and a traitor. But I'm a coward who survived. That's a skill. I'll teach it.
85.done: You've got all my moves! I'd ask you not to tell Vegeta, but apparently he doesn't even remember my name.

86.greet: Lesson one: the pose. Lesson two: the pose. Lesson three: also the pose. Then we'll get to the punching.
86.done: Magnificent! Your pose is nearly as fine as mine! Welcome to the Ginyu Force, honorary member!

87.greet: Recoome teach you! First, the Recoome Fighting Pose! No, bigger! BIGGER!
87.done: You learned the Recoome Eraser Gun! Recoome so proud! Recoome will hug you! ...Too late to run.

88.greet: Speed is everything, and nobody in the universe is faster than me. So try not to blink.
88.done: Fast. Almost as fast as me. Almost. Don't get cocky.

89.greet: Right then, mate. The Crusher Ball's all in the wrist. And the attitude. Mostly the attitude.
89.done: Brilliant! The Red Magma himself would be proud. That's me, by the way. I'm the Red Magma.

90.greet: I can stop time! Only while I'm holding my breath. So we're doing lessons in very, very short chunks.
90.done: You learned everything! Wow. Nobody ever finishes my lessons. Usually they just leave.

91.greet: You wish to learn from me? How flattering. Very well. Do try not to die in the first lesson. It's so untidy.
91.done: You've learned all I care to teach in this form. Consider yourself fortunate. Most of my students are dust.

92.greet: Ah, my second form. Bigger, cruder, more fun. Let's see how long you last against the horns.
92.done: Splendid. You may now say you survived lessons from a tyrant. Do use that line at parties.

93.greet: This shape disgusts even me. That is rather the point. Fear is a technique, and I am its master.
93.done: Hmph. You barely flinched. Irritating. Very well, you have your lessons.

96.greet: Half metal, all resentment. I learned to fight again from scratch after that wretched monkey. Now so will you.
96.done: There. Every lesson. Remember: a tyrant never truly dies. He simply gets upgraded.

97.greet: Kneel. No? Hmph. Then stand, and learn how a true monarch fights. With dignity, and a sword when available.
97.done: You fight with nearly royal poise. My sons could have learned from you. They never learned from anyone.

98.greet: Frieza Force basic training! Step one: scout. Step two: report. Step three: run if the number is too high.
98.done: You passed! Better than I did. I failed step three. Very painfully.

99.greet: The Life-Risking Blow is the only special move they ever taught us. It's right there in the name. Ready?
99.done: That's all the Frieza Force ever taught me. Short course. Most of us didn't graduate.

148.greet: My rates are high, but for you, a special discount. The Dodon-Pa first. Point your finger like a gun.
148.done: Hmph. You'd make a passable assassin. You'd make a better one if you smiled less.

149.greet: This steel body taught me patience. And grudges. You'll learn both, along with the Hidden Blade.
149.done: You've learned it all. Now leave. My arm-blade gets itchy around good students.

150.greet: Discipline! Posture! Mind over matter! And absolutely no talking penguins near the training ground!
150.done: You have the makings of a fine soldier. And if you ever see a girl in glasses, you never met me.

151.greet: My Devilmite Beam only harms the wicked. Let's see how much of it hurts you. Hohoho.
151.done: You barely flinched at my beam! Disappointing for me, wonderful for you. Off you go.

152.greet: Lessons from the future ruler of the world? Ha! Fine, but you're polishing the robot afterward.
152.done: You learned everything! Now swear loyalty to Emperor Pilaf! No? Ugh. Nobody ever swears loyalty.

153.greet: Mai! Shu! Combine! Behold the ultimate machine! You're learning from the absolute peak of engineering!
153.done: You beat the course! We're low on missiles anyway. Go away before Mai sees the repair bill.

154.greet: The Demon King's son trains no one gently. I'll teach you the Soumasen the way I learned it: by surviving it.
154.done: You survived every lesson. My father would have eaten you for your insolence. I think I'll let you live.

155.greet: I am the Demon King. Rulers do not teach; they command. So I command you to learn. Begin.
155.done: You have learned the Demon King's arts. Use them to rule, or be ruled. There is no third way.

156.greet: Ncha! Training time! First we run around the planet. Kidding! Twice! Kidding! Okay, let's go!
156.done: You learned all my moves! Now you're the second-strongest person in Penguin Village! Ncha!

157.greet: I won't go easy on you just because you're the Patrol's darling. I raised two Saiyans and I'm still standing. Stance!
157.done: You're done! Now go eat something. You look thin. Everyone looks thin to me, but you especially.
